about: Test sentences for 'ask in English everywhere' (round 10, part B; step 10-6) and the exact action each should turn into. Written 2026-10-09, before any prompt, schema or engine existed, and never edited to suit a model's answer (new sentences may be added later, marked with their date). 'dev' sentences may be used to tune the prompt; 'test' sentences are scored once at the end, three runs, with the prompt chosen on 'dev' (step 10-7 writes the result to api/ask_eval.json). They are written the way strangers type: nicknames, typos, 'this season', bare names. The engine's job is to turn a sentence into something the app already does: open a page with its inputs, build a Workbench board, run the Player Finder, open a live game, ask which namesake, or refuse with a reason. It never writes SQL or a URL of its own.

open_page.scored: page and hash equal; params equal as a whole after normalisation (below); a key the sentence didn't ask for is wrong, except the free keys: compare's a and b (names beside aid/bid), shotcharts' player (a name beside pid), and pg (paging) on any page. No params = {} (the page's own defaults apply).

build_board.scored: the sets equal (kinds, and ids/codes as sets); every expected block is matched by one produced block of the same type whose every named key is equal (expected columns must all be among the produced columns; a finder block's spec is compared as run_finder is). Blocks the expected doesn't name (notes, set blocks, extra tables, charts or tools on the same sets) are not penalised. A key the expected block doesn't name (the season range, the columns) is free.

shape.flag: <true when something in the sentence can't go in the boxes and must be said>
shape.spec: <the Player Finder spec of api/workbench_parse_sentences.json: dataset, scope, season_from, season_to, min_games, filters, conditions>

run_finder.scored: exactly as the Finder's English box is scored (scripts/workbench_parse_eval.py): data set, scope, seasons, games floor, filters, conditions as a set, and the flag, both sides after workbench_parse_lib.finalize().

shape.team: <today's code, or null for the list of today's games>

open_live_game.scored: team equal (null = none). What the live page shows when the team has no game today is the page's business.

shape.name: <the typed name>
shape.then: <the action to run once one is chosen (documentation only)>

ask.scored: about and the set of options equal: a name that belongs to two players on file is asked about, never guessed.

normalisation: Numbers compare as numbers (a URL's '10' = 10); other strings trimmed, case- and accent-insensitive; team codes upper-case.

List-valued keys (gamefinder f, statline line, breakouts stats, plays per, builder w) compare as sets of their comma-separated items; a Game Finder condition is stat:op:value, a stat line item stat:value (percentages as shares, 0.65 = 65%).

Season tokens: 'current' = api/current_season.status()['current'] on the day the evaluation runs (2025-26 until the first 2026-27 final is stored, then 2026-27); 'last' = status()['latest_complete'] (2025-26 either way this autumn); 'current-N' = current minus N. Seasons are end years (2022-23 = 2023). On the shotcharts page a season is its label ('2015-16'): a token is resolved, then written as a label.
Date tokens: 'yesterday' = the NBA date before today's (US Eastern, utils/date.js nbaDateIso()). Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.

Player ids are NBA ids as player_season_stats has them (the app's own search, GET /workbench/entities, resolves names, accents ignored). The 'players' field on a sentence documents the ids and is not scored.
rules: Seasons: end years; a bare year Y is the season ending in Y ('in 2010' = 2009-10); 'this season' / 'this year' = current; 'last season' = last; 'next season' / 'next year' on a projection = the projections page (it has one target season); 'ever' / 'of all time' on a leaderboard = 1950 (the data's first season) to current; a decade ('the 1990s') = the seasons ending in its years (1990 to 1999); 'as a rookie' = the player's first season on file; 'since 2015-16' = from 2016 with no upper bound.

Players: resolved by NBA id. Nicknames and misspellings go to the one player they commonly mean (Steph, Klay, Bron/LeBron, KD, Luka, Giannis, Wemby, Shai/SGA, Dame, Shaq, MJ, Dirk, Kobe, Magic, Wilt, Ant, Book, Joker). A name that belongs to two players on file ('Mike James', 'Brandon Williams', 'Reggie Williams', 'Eddie Johnson' and 15 more) is asked about, never guessed.

Teams: today's NBA codes, from nicknames, cities and short forms (Dubs = GSW, Sixers = PHI, Blazers = POR, Wolves = MIN, Cavs = CLE, Mavs = DAL, OKC, Philly). A franchise's past season uses today's code (the team page and the catalogue map old codes).

Which action: one player, one team or one tool with inputs = open_page with only what the sentence gives (the page's defaults fill the rest). Two players compared = the Player Comparison page. Three or more players, two or more teams, a named chart, or named stats to lay side by side = build_board (a set plus a table, or a chart). A list of players meeting conditions = run_finder. A list of single games (one player's N-point games, all 60-point games, a streak of games) = the Game Finder page (f = stat:op:value). 'Seasons like 27/7/7' = the Stat Line Finder. A stat's leaders in a season or range, with an optional team = the Leaderboard Builder (Stat Leaders has no URL inputs). A score 'right now' / 'tonight' / 'live' = open_live_game. A past date's games = Live Scores with the date; 'today' needs no date.

Per-player blocks (game log, next-season projection, on/off, RAPM, clutch, contract, shot zones) live on the Player Profile: a player's X with no page named opens his profile. A team's on/off, pairs and lineups are Analytics tabs (?page=analytics#onoff etc.) with the team and season filled; a team's rotation, assist network, possessions and coaching decisions have their own pages with a team key.
Shot Charts: the player by pid, the season as a label, games = 'playoffs' or 'all' only when said (regular season is the default), view = heatmap / shotmaking / quality / value only when said.

The Finder's rules hold for run_finder (api/workbench_parse_sentences.json 'rules'): game logs when single games are needed, else season stats; one result per player-season when a season is named or implied, combined over seasons for 'since', 'straight', 'ever'; 'averaged 20' = at least 20; a triple-double = 10+ points, rebounds and assists; positions, rookies, awards and 'or' can't go in the boxes and are reported with the rest filled (flag). A team filter on a season average ('for the Knicks') goes to the Leaderboard Builder's team box instead.

The data's edges are known: game logs and every play-by-play tool (Game Finder, Play Finder, rotations, assist networks, on/off, RAPM, lineups, pairs, possessions, coaching, replay, clutch, hot streaks, splits, best games) start in 2020-21; shot locations in 1996-97; player seasons in 1949-50; team seasons in 1946-47; salaries end with 2024-25. An ask outside an edge is refused with no_data, never answered with the nearest season the data has.
Nothing is filled that the sentence doesn't say: no view, sort, floor, limit or extra condition the person didn't ask for.
Refusals are plain and carry one of the reasons below; the normal search still works. Comparing two players is not an opinion (it opens the comparison); 'who is the GOAT' is.

refusal_reasons.off_topic: not a question about basketball data in this app (weather, poems, app settings)
refusal_reasons.opinion: a judgement with no stat behind it ('who is the GOAT'); the app shows numbers, it doesn't rank greatness
refusal_reasons.other_league: WNBA, EuroLeague, G League, international play: not on file
refusal_reasons.no_data: the kind of thing the app has, but not for that season, player or span (see the data's edges in the rules)
refusal_reasons.unknown_player: nobody of that name on file (after the app's own search, accents ignored)
refusal_reasons.needs_a_computed_answer: the answer is a number no page shows ('the average age of MVP winners'): the parked 'Ask the Database' (B5), not this box
refusal_reasons.would_change_data: asks to add, edit or delete data; the box only reads
refusal_reasons.betting_advice: asks what to bet; the app shows markets against its model, never advice (owner's decision, 2026-10-03)
